subject: Testing Strict versus scalar invariance in lavaan.mi and getting same result

messages.author: 13b33ee9ca077816
messages.subject: Testing Strict versus scalar invariance in lavaan.mi and getting same result
parts:
Hi, I am trying to test strict versus scalar invariance with a cfa model using imputed data and lavaan.mi.  I'm getting the same results when I use group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts") as I am with group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals"). 

This is my code:

###############################
#Scalar invariance
###############################
fit_scalar<- cfa.mi(modeloverall, data = impList, ordered=TRUE, group="sex", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"), estimator="DWLS", se="robust", test="scaled.shifted")
summary(fit_scalar, fit.measures=T, standardized=TRUE)

###############################
#Very Strong invariance
###############################
fit_verystrong<- cfa.mi(modeloverall, data = impList, ordered=TRUE, group="sex", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals"), estimator="DWLS", se="robust", test="scaled.shifted")
summary(fit_verystrong, fit.measures=T, standardized=TRUE)

Is it possible that there is a bug in lavaan.mi for this? 

Thanks,
Steph

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Testing Strict versus scalar invariance in lavaan.mi and getting same result
parts:
Hi, Steph,

Lavaan's default is to use delta parameterization, which does not model the residuals of ordinal variables.
To test strict invariance, you have to change to theta parameterization, although I've never seen anyone suggesting its use.

Suggestions about how to test invariance measurement with ordinal data:
https://doi.org/10.7275/qazy-2946
measurement invariance for ordinal variables (google.com)

Best,
Yago
